ai.literal: Knowing virtue, mature, wisdom-possessing people's friendship, knowing the proper way, and having deliberated, acquiring.
ai.translation: One should secure the friendship of wise and mature people who know what is right, by understanding the proper means and carefully deliberating.
ai.modern: அறநெறியை அறிந்து முதிர்ந்த அறிவுடையவர்களின் நட்பை, அதற்கான வழியை அறிந்து ஆராய்ந்து ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of gaining the friendship of wise, mature elders who understand virtue. The poet advises that such valuable associations cannot be acquired casually; one must understand the proper approach (tiran) and carefully evaluate (terntu) how to secure their companionship (kolal). The word 'mutta' refers to maturity in both age and wisdom, while 'kenmai' signifies a deep, supportive friendship.

ai.literal: Arisen affliction removing, [future affliction] not happening beforehand protecting, those of [such] character, cherishing, acquiring.
ai.translation: To cherish and secure the friendship of those who can dispel existing troubles and guard against future ones before they occur.
ai.modern: வந்துள்ள துன்பத்தை நீக்கி, இனிமேல் துன்பம் வராமல் முன்னதாகவே காக்கும் தன்மை உடைய பெரியோர்களைப் போற்றித் துணையாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the essential qualities of the wise guides whom a leader should seek as companions. They possess two key abilities: first, they can resolve and remove troubles that have already occurred; second, they can foresee and prevent future difficulties before they arise. A wise ruler must cherish and secure the guidance of such capable mentors to ensure steady and safe governance.

ai.literal: Among all rare things, the rarest indeed is, great people, cherishing, as one's own, securing.
ai.translation: Of all rare blessings, the rarest of all is to cherish great people and secure them as one's own kin.
ai.modern: அடைவதற்கரிய நன்மைகள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் மிகவும் அரிய நன்மை, பெரியவர்களைப் போற்றி அவர்களைத் நமக்குச் சுற்றத்தாராக ஆக்கிக் கொள்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of securing the guidance of wise elders. The author compares this to all other rare achievements in life and declares it to be the most difficult and valuable of all. The key words 'பேணி' (cherishing) and 'தமராக் கொளல்' (making them one's own) show that this is not a casual association; it requires active respect, honor, and cultivation to turn wise mentors into close allies.

ai.literal: Behaving with those who are greater than oneself as one's own people is, among all strengths, the foremost.
ai.translation: To live in close association with those who are greater than oneself, making them one's own allies, is the supreme power among all powers.
ai.modern: தன்னைவிட அறிவு ஒழுக்கங்களில் பெரியவர்களைத் தன் உறவினராகக் கொண்டு அவரோடு கூடி வாழ்வது, ஒருவனுக்கு உள்ள எல்லா வலிமைகளுள்ளும் முதன்மையான வலிமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of securing the friendship of wise and virtuous elders. The term 'tammiṉ periyār' refers to people who excel in wisdom, character, and experience. By treating them as 'tamar' (one's own close kin or allies) and acting according to their guidance, a person gains a protective shield. The poet declares that this social and moral alliance is 'vaṉmaiyuḷ ellām talai'—the greatest of all strengths, far exceeding physical force, wealth, or military power.

ai.literal: Because of conducting oneself with those who deliberate as eyes, the king, those who deliberate, having examined, should secure.
ai.translation: Since a king must conduct his affairs with wise counselors acting as his eyes, he should carefully examine and secure such advisors for himself.
ai.modern: ஆலோசிப்பவர்களைத் தன் கண்களாகக் கொண்டு அரசன் செயல்பட வேண்டும் என்பதால், அவன் அத்தகைய ஆலோசிப்பவர்களை ஆராய்ந்து தன் துணையாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the indispensable role of wise advisors in governance. The poet uses the metaphor of 'eyes' (கண்) for counselors (சூழ்வார்), showing that a ruler cannot navigate statecraft blindly. Since a king must act based on the vision provided by these 'eyes', he must put great effort into choosing them. Therefore, the ruler is urged to carefully examine (சூழ்ந்து) and secure (கொளல்) the companionship of truly wise and deliberative people.

ai.literal: To him who is capable of conducting himself with worthy people as his association, there is nothing remaining for enemies to do.
ai.translation: For one who is capable of conducting his life with the guidance and association of worthy people, there is nothing that enemies can do to harm him.
ai.modern: தகுதியுடைய பெரியோர்களைத் தன் துணையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ வல்லவனுக்கு, அவனுடைய பகைவர்கள் செய்யக்கூடிய தீங்கு என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute protection gained by surrounding oneself with wise and virtuous guides. The word 'takkār' refers to worthy or fit people, and 'iṉattaṉāy' means making them one's close circle or association. When a person is capable ('vallāṉai') of conducting ('oḻuka') their life under such guidance, they leave no room for errors. Consequently, there is absolutely nothing ('il') left for enemies ('ceṟṟār') to do ('ceya') to harm them, as the collective wisdom of their companions shields them from all vulnerabilities.

ai.literal: Those who secure the supportive companions who reprove, who indeed are they with the capability of ruining them?
ai.translation: Who indeed has the power to ruin those who secure the guidance of companions who have the courage to reprove them when they err?
ai.modern: தவறு செய்யும்போது கடிந்து அறிவுரை கூறும் பெரியோர்களைத் துணையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்பவர்களை அழிக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர் யார் இருக்கிறார்கள்?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme protection gained by keeping wise and honest companions. The word 'இடிக்கும்' means to sharply reprove or admonish, describing friends who do not hesitate to point out one's faults. Those who 'secure' (ஆள்வரை) such companions are shielded from moral and political downfall. The rhetorical question asks who could possibly have the power to ruin such a person, emphasizing that sincere, critical guidance makes one invincible.

ai.literal: A king who does not have those who reprove him, being unprotected, will perish even if he has no one to destroy him.
ai.translation: A king who lacks the guidance of those who can openly reprove his faults is unprotected and will ruin himself, even if he has no enemies to destroy him.
ai.modern: தவறு செய்யும்போது கடிந்து அறிவுரை கூறும் பெரியோர்களைத் துணையாகக் கொள்ளாத, பாதுகாப்பற்ற மன்னன், தன்னை அழிக்கும் பகைவர் யாரும் இல்லாவிட்டாலும் தானே அழிந்துவிடுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the vital role of wise counselors who have the courage to criticize and correct a ruler's mistakes. The word 'இடிப்பாரை' refers to those who reprove or admonish with harsh but necessary truths. A king without such guides is described as 'ஏமரா' (unprotected), meaning he lacks a defensive shield against his own errors. Even in the absence of external enemies ('கெடுப்பார் இலானும்'), his own unchecked missteps will inevitably lead to his downfall ('கெடும்'). Thus, honest criticism is presented not as a threat, but as an essential safeguard for leadership.

ai.literal: To those who have no capital, there is no profit; to those who have no support that acts as a prop, there is no stability.
ai.translation: Just as there is no profit for those who have no capital, there is no stability for those who lack the support of a strong prop.
ai.modern: முதலீடு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு லாபம் இல்லை; அதுபோல, தாங்கிப் பிடிக்கும் தூண் போன்ற பெரியோரின் ஆதரவு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு வாழ்வில் நிலைத்தன்மை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple financial analogy to explain the necessity of having wise and strong companions. Just as a merchant cannot earn any profit without an initial capital investment, a person cannot achieve stability or security in life without a strong supporting prop. Here, the supporting prop refers to the guidance and protection of wise elders. Without such a safeguard, one's position and endeavors will easily collapse.

ai.literal: Than incurring the enmity of many people, abandoning the friendship of the good is ten-fold harmful.
ai.translation: Abandoning the friendship of the wise and good is ten times more harmful than incurring the enmity of many foes.
ai.modern: பலருடைய பகையைத் தேடிக்கொள்வதை விட, நல்லவர்களின் நட்பைக் கைவிடுவது பத்து மடங்கு அதிகத் தீமையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the vital importance of retaining the support of wise and virtuous guides. The poet compares two undesirable situations: earning the hostility of many people and losing the friendship of the good. He declares that abandoning (விடல்) the association (தொடர்கை) of the wise (நல்லார்) is ten times (பத்தடுத்த) more ruinous (தீமைத்தே) than making many enemies (பல்லார் பகை). Without the guidance of the wise, one is left completely vulnerable to errors, making the loss of their friendship far more dangerous than any external opposition.
